title: Where can you find free practice cases from the consulting firms themselves?
description: A list of the free, official practice cases and interview guides published by McKinsey, BCG, Bain, Deloitte and other firms, and how to use them.
hook: The best free practice cases come straight from the firms: McKinsey, Bain, Deloitte and Oliver Wyman all publish sample cases on their careers sites, and BCG offers interview tips and a free virtual job simulation. Official material shows you how each firm frames a problem and what it expects from a candidate. Here is what each firm offers as of November 2026, and how to get three practice sessions out of every case.

Why official material is worth your time

Official cases are short, and there are not many of them, so they will not replace a casebook. Their value is different: they show how a firm frames a problem, what kind of data it hands over and what it calls a good answer. Reading a firm's own advice on its interviews also tells you which skills it emphasises, which helps with "why this firm?" questions. Start with the firms you are applying to, then use your wider practice to build volume.

Firms update these pages often. Everything below was checked in November 2026; always go to the firm's own careers site for the current version.

McKinsey

McKinsey's interviewing page explains its problem-solving interview (its name for the case interview), the personal experience interview and the Solve assessment. It includes five practice cases with suggested approaches:

  • Beautify: whether a global beauty company should train its in-store consultants to sell through virtual channels.
  • Diconsa: using a Mexican network of rural stores to offer basic financial services, for a foundation client.
  • Electro-Light: launching a reduced-sugar sports drink for a beverage company.
  • Transforming a national education system: diagnosing and improving a country's schools.
  • Talbot Trucks: whether a European truck maker should invest in electric trucks.

The cases move question by question, which suits practising for interviewer-led cases. McKinsey's page also asks candidates to tailor their approach rather than apply standard frameworks, which is good advice for any firm. For more on the process, see the McKinsey interview process.

BCG

BCG's case interview preparation page explains what a BCG case involves (structuring, asking questions, analysing data, quick calculations) and lists do's and don'ts such as thinking structurally, clarifying assumptions and not staying silent. It links to OneDay@BCG, a free virtual job simulation of a consultant's work, and to an article on what BCG looks for in case interviews. As of November 2026 it does not host a library of practice cases, so use the tips to shape how you practise and use other cases for volume. The BCG interview process covers the rounds, including the online case.

Bain

Bain's case interview page describes the case as a structured conversation about a real business problem and gives tips for in-person and virtual interviews. It offers two practice cases:

  • Coffee Shop Co.: whether a friend should open a coffee shop, a good first case for profitability and break-even.
  • FashionCo.: why a fashion company's revenue has declined for five years, a classic revenue-drop diagnosis.

The page also lists several external prep providers that Bain points candidates to. See the Bain interview process for the rest of the process.

Deloitte

Deloitte runs a free, interactive case interview practice tool, plus a case interview tips page. The tool is useful because you work through a case step by step rather than just reading it. Deloitte's processes vary by country and service line, so read the Deloitte interview process alongside it.

Oliver Wyman and other firms

Oliver Wyman's interview preparation page includes sample cases, such as an oil and gas pricing strategy case. Many other strategy and consulting firms publish tips or sample cases too. The quickest way to find them is to search the firm's own careers site for "case interview" or "interview preparation". Prefer material on the firm's own domain; copies elsewhere are often out of date.

Which material to use for what

If you want to practiseUseWhy
Interviewer-led casesMcKinsey's practice casesEach question stands on its own, as in the real format
Driving a case yourselfBain's Coffee Shop Co. and FashionCo.Open prompts where you choose what to look at next
Working through a case step by stepDeloitte's interactive toolYou respond at each stage instead of just reading
Understanding the job itselfOneDay@BCGUseful material for "why consulting?" answers
Pricing casesOliver Wyman's sample casesIncludes an oil and gas pricing strategy case

Whatever you choose, keep a note of which case types you have covered so that your practice is not all one shape.

Turn one official case into three practice sessions

You will get more from one official case worked properly than from skimming ten.

Pass 1: solve it cold

Before reading any suggested answer, do the case out loud and timed. Write your recap, structure, calculations and final recommendation.

Pass 2: compare carefully

Set your answer beside the firm's. Label each difference as missing logic, weaker prioritisation or a different but valid approach. Not every difference is a mistake.

Pass 3: make it a mock interview and stretch it

Give the case to a partner, who reveals information only when you ask for it and pushes you to explain what every number means. Then change the assumptions and see whether your answer survives.

For example, say a case concludes that a market can support five stores: the client can capture 25% of $40M of local spending, which is $10M, and each store needs $2M of revenue to break even. Ask yourself what happens if revenue comes in 15% lower: $8.5M supports only four stores. If the client wins half the expected share, $5M supports two. Then say whether the recommendation changes. That turns a one-off case into practice in judgement, which is what the interview tests.

Mistakes people make with official cases

  • Reading the answer first. Once you have seen it, you cannot test yourself on that case again.
  • Treating the suggested answer as the only answer. The firms themselves say there is no single right answer.
  • Only practising one firm's style. Most candidates apply to several firms. Practise interviewer-led and candidate-led cases.
  • Relying on old copies. Third-party collections often show retired cases. Use the firm's current page.

Check yourself

1. You have interviews at McKinsey and Bain in three weeks. Which official cases do you do first?

Show the answer

One McKinsey case (to practise the interviewer-led, question-by-question style) and Bain's Coffee Shop Co. or FashionCo. (to practise driving a case yourself). Do each cold, then as a mock with a partner.

2. In the store example, how many stores could the market support if the client captured 30% of $40M?

Show the answer

30% × $40M = $12M. At $2M per store, that supports six stores.

Where to practise next

When you have used the official cases, the PrepForCase casebook has over 100 cases with worked answers and interviewer scripts, and the drills train the individual skills. For other books and tools, see the best case interview books and case prep websites and tools.
